title: Putin boasts 'most powerful missile in the world' after test
text:

Russia announces it has successfully tested a new generation of nuclear-capable missiles that it says can rival its Western counterparts, although Western analysts say claims are exaggerated, according to Reuters.
Board of peace envoy delivers stark warning on Gaza’s future The official in charge of implementing the US-brokered ceasefire deal in Gaza warned on Wednesday that failure to advance the agreement risks entrenching “a dangerous status quo.
” Referring to Israel’s “yellow line” of separation in Gaza that continues to expand, Nickolay Mladenov said failing to advance the next phases of the ceasefire would entrench Israel’s long-term presence in Gaza and leave two million Palestinians without a viable future. Mladenov held his first briefing with the press in Jerusalem, where CNN’s Jeremy Diamond analyzed his remarks.
A Palestinian teenager was shot dead by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank in the presence of the Israeli military on Wednesday morning, according to the mayor of the town and Israeli human rights group B’Tselem. Eyewitnesses told CNN a group of settlers drove into the towns of Jilijliya and Sinjil Wednesday morning, stealing hundreds of sheep, while assaulting residents.
The Israeli military said the incident is under review, and they are “aware of reports” of what they described as “suspects” who were injured and killed, but claimed it was Palestinians who stole livestock from the illegal outpost. CNN’s Jeremy Diamond reports. Gunshots were heard from inside the Philippine Senate compound. No casualties have been reported and the incident is still being investigated as armed forces have since entered the building.
This comes just days after Senator Ronald Dela Rosa was seen running away from local agents through the halls of the Senate. Prosecutors at the International Criminal Court issued a warrant for his arrest accused him of conspiring with former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte in alleged crimes against humanity. CNN's long journey to reach Iran's capital CNN's Matthew Chance reports from northwestern Iran, where he and his team are driving to Tehran.
The journey is taking much longer than usual since infrastructure has been destroyed in US-Israeli strikes. CNN operates in Iran with the permission of the Iranian government, as required under local regulations, but maintains full editorial control over what it reports. CNN's photojournalist Alex Platt contributed to this report. US President Donald Trump arrived in China’s capital with over a dozen high-profile business leaders, including Apple's Tim Cook and Tesla CEO Elon Musk.
CNN's Clare Duffy digs into why and who were among those on Air Force One. President Donald Trump was welcomed in China’s capital with pomp and pageantry for the start of a crucial visit carrying global consequences, as the world’s two largest economies frame their trade relationship. CNN's Kristen Holmes reports from Beijing. Viral videos of rats inside Taipei shopping malls, markets and train stations are fueling public anxiety after Taiwan recorded its first hantavirus death in 25 years.
As rat sightings spread across social media, city officials are ramping up poison traps, street cleanings and disinfection campaigns across Taiwan’s capital. CNN’s Will Ripley reports. Authorities in eastern France are warning drivers to stay vigilant in wooded areas after saying wild animals may behave unpredictably after consuming fermented fruit or decomposing vegetation.
Former Philippines police chief Ronald dela Rosa, who oversaw former President Rodrigo Duterte’s deadly drug war, locked himself in his Senate office after the ICC unsealed a warrant accusing him of crimes against humanity. Dela Rosa, named a co‑conspirator in Duterte’s case, is under Senate protection while urging President Marcos not to hand him over to the Hague.
President Donald Trump had hoped to focus on US economic priorities with Chinese President Xi Jinping, but the Iran war — and his failed efforts at a peace deal — will complicate the US president’s prior goals. CNN's Betsy Klein reports from Beijing. The assassination of Francisco Beltran, an alleged cartel operative, on a Mexican highway in March was facilitated by American CIA officers.
According to multiple sources, it was part of an expanded and previously unreported CIA operation inside the country. The CIA declined to comment when first informed of CNN's reporting, but then called it a"PR stunt" for the cartel after it published. CNN’s Natasha Bertrand reports.
